title: THE RUNGS · JERK SCHOOL + THE CROSSING LADDER
vibe: GREEN · 7 hours, nothing sore, a day off in the bank, and you said go hard. So today is built on rungs. Nothing today is counted in minutes — you count rungs, you count ladders, you count quarters of a mile. Two things get fixed: the jerk you never actually found, and the fact that this program has never once put you on the floor.
why: Three things drove today. First, the jerk. On July 27th you ran all eight rounds of the Olympic chain and push-pressed every single one — you never found the second dip, and grip was the thing that failed, not lungs. That is not a strength problem, it is a timing problem, and timing cannot be learned in round four of a chain when your hands are going. So the jerk gets its own slot today, first, cold, with full rest and no clock on it. There are three dips in a jerk, not one: dip and drive, then dip UNDER the bells and lock, then dip to catch. The middle one is the one you have been skipping, and the drill for it is the half jerk — springy quarter squats where you launch the bells with your legs and let them float. That is what block one is. Second, the climb. You told me the one-way version on the 2nd felt about the same as the pyramid on the 27th, and that is real information: half a mile per hour faster, two more minutes at steep grade and no descent to hide in still landed inside your noise. Incline is not done working, the step was just too small — so it comes back later as a genuinely bigger jump, not another half-measure, and today goes flat and fast instead. Third, the hole. Every session in this log is bells, treadmill, or floor core. You have never done a push-up. Not one, in a month of training. Today the ladder runs two directions at once — the bells climb from one rep to five while the push-ups fall from ten down to two — so the block gets harder and easier at the same time and you never know which half is going to call it. That shape has never been in this program, and it puts your own bodyweight in the session for the first time.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP · SHOULDERS, SPINE, WRISTS
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day A · rotated off Sunday's Day B · this is an overhead day, so it is built at the lockout
blocks.text: Everything today ends with something locked out over your head or your hands on the floor. Build both. Move continuously: shoulder dislocates with a towel or belt x15, go wider than feels necessary · thoracic rotations on all fours, 8 per side, reach for the ceiling and follow your hand with your eyes · Jefferson curl, roll down and back up slowly, x5 · single-leg goodmorning 8/side · active pigeon 30s/side · horse-stance squat hold 30s · wrist rocks and circles 15 each direction, then load your wrists — hands flat on the floor, rock forward and back 10 times, then flip to the backs of your hands and do 10 more. That last one is not optional today, you are about to do ninety push-ups. Finish with an overhead lockout check: clean one 40 to the rack, press it up, and hold it dead still for 20 seconds each side. Biceps beside the ear. If it will not get there, spend another 30 seconds on dislocates.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · JERK SCHOOL
blocks.meta: ~7 min · 2×40 lb · SKILL WORK, NOT CONDITIONING · full rest, low reps, no clock
blocks.format: SKILL BLOCK · three progressions, ~3 sets each · stop every set while it still looks good
blocks.workRest: This is the lightest-feeling block in the session and it is the most important one. You are here to find the SECOND DIP — the one where you drop UNDER the bells and lock your elbows, rather than pressing the bells up to your arms. Rest as long as you want between sets. If a rep turns into a push press, that set is over, no exceptions. Do not chase reps, do not get out of breath, do not try to make this hard. You have eight rounds of evidence from July 27th that you can grind this pattern; what you have zero evidence of is that you can time it. Total work here is maybe twenty reps.

items.name: 1 · HALF JERKS × 5, three sets (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 2×40 lb, clean to the rack. NEW — never been in your log. Springy quarter squat, then LAUNCH the bells off your chest with your legs and let them float up to about head height. Arms stay relaxed, they are ropes, not pistons. Heels can come off the floor on the drive. You are not locking anything out — you are just learning what it feels like when your legs throw the bells and your arms do nothing. Catch soft, dip your knees, go again. Five reps, three sets, rest as needed.

items.name: 2 · PAUSED JERKS × 3, three sets
items.detail: 2×40 lb. Now add the part you have been missing. Dip and drive — then DROP UNDER the bells and lock your elbows out while you are still sinking, and FREEZE there in the quarter squat with arms locked overhead for a full two seconds. That frozen position is the second dip. Then stand up out of it. Then dip and catch back to the rack. Three reps a set, and the pause is the whole point — if you are standing up before your elbows are locked, you are still push-pressing.

items.name: 3 · FULL JERKS × 2, three sets
items.detail: 2×40 lb. Put it together at speed: dip, drive, dip and lock, stand, dip and catch. Five steps, one continuous motion. Two reps a set. If the timing falls apart, go back to paused jerks and finish there — that is a successful session, not a failed one. THE QUESTION FOR TODAY: did the bells ever feel weightless at the top of the drive? That floating moment is what you are hunting for, and it is the only report that matters out of this block.

blocks.text: The July 27th chain proved you can move 80 pounds overhead for eight rounds. It also proved you do it with your shoulders instead of your legs, which is why your grip died before your lungs did — a push press keeps the bells in your hands longer and under tension longer than a jerk does. Fix the timing and the same work costs you less. That is what this seven minutes buys.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE RUN LADDER
blocks.meta: ~15 min · treadmill · 0% incline · measured in DISTANCE, not minutes · each rung is shorter and faster than the last
blocks.format: DESCENDING DISTANCE / ASCENDING SPEED · 3 rungs · 1.5 mi of work + 2 easy floats
blocks.workRest: Three rungs. Each one is half the distance of the one before it and a notch faster. Watch the distance readout, not the clock — this is the first run in your log counted in miles instead of minutes, and that is deliberate. Reset the trip distance or just do the math off the running total, whichever is easier. Floats are 90 seconds at 6.0, easy, keep your feet moving. Cadence 168 to 172 the whole way, short quick steps. Flat today on purpose: you told me the one-way climb landed about the same as the pyramid, so incline is going to come back as a real jump rather than another half-step, and in the meantime this is the fastest quarter mile that has ever been on your plan.

items.name: RUNG 1 · 0.75 mi @ 7.8
items.detail: About 5:45. Comfortably hard — this is the pace you should be able to hold and still count it as work rather than a race. Settle in early, do not go out chasing it. Get your cadence quick from the first step so you are not correcting it later.

items.name: FLOAT · 90 sec @ 6.0
items.detail: Easy. Keep running, do not walk. Breathe on a rhythm and let your heart rate come down a little, but this is a float, not a rest — you should be ready to go again the second it ends.

items.name: RUNG 2 · 0.5 mi @ 8.2
items.detail: About 3:40. Half the distance, faster belt. This one should feel like a proper tempo — breathing hard, form still clean, no flailing. Two laps of a track's worth. Stay tall through the middle when it starts to bite.

items.name: FLOAT · 90 sec @ 6.0
items.detail: Same as before. Easy legs, quick feet, get your breath organized. The next rung is short and it is the whole point of the block, so arrive at it ready.

items.name: RUNG 3 · 0.25 mi @ 8.8
items.detail: About 1:42. The fastest sustained prescription you have had — you hit 9.0 for 30-second reps in the Mona fartlek on the 28th and did not remark on it, so a quarter mile at 8.8 should be inside your range but it will not be comfortable at the end. One lap. Do not touch the belt, just hold on and finish it. THIS IS THE BENCHMARK OF THE DAY — report what it felt like at the 200-meter mark.

items.name: WALK DOWN · 60 sec @ 3.0
items.detail: Drop to a walk immediately and stay on the belt for a full minute. Do not step off and stand still after a quarter at 8.8.

blocks.text: Your last four run prescriptions: a descending fartlek, two baseline flat miles, an 18-minute aerobic block you extended to 21 on your own, and Sunday's climb. Every one of them counted in time. This one counts in distance, gets shorter as it gets faster, and sits in the MIDDLE of the session instead of at either end — which means you go into the bells already tired. That is on purpose. The ladder after this is a density block, not a strength block; degraded output is the intended condition.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · THE CROSSING LADDER
blocks.meta: ~13 min · 2×40 lb + bodyweight · bells climb 1→5, push-ups fall 10→2 · count LADDERS, not minutes
blocks.format: CROSSING LADDER · 5 rungs per ladder · 15 clean & push press + 30 push-ups per ladder · repeat from rung 1
blocks.workRest: One ladder is five rungs. On every rung the bells go UP by one rep and the push-ups come DOWN by two. Finish rung five, go straight back to rung one, and start again. Rest only when you need it, and take it between rungs rather than mid-rung. 13-minute cap. GREEN target is 3 complete ladders — that is 45 double clean and push press at 80 pounds and 90 push-ups. YELLOW is 2. Do NOT jerk in this block. You just spent seven minutes learning that timing and it will not survive a heart rate this high — push press it deliberately, arms and legs together, and keep the jerk clean in your memory for next time.

items.name: RUNG 1 · 1 clean & push press + 10 push-ups
items.detail: 2×40 lb. Clean both bells from the floor to the rack, dip, push press overhead, lower to the rack, lower to the floor. That is one rep. Then straight to the floor for 10 push-ups — chest to the deck, full lockout at the top, no sagging hips. First push-ups in this program, so set the standard here and hold it.

items.name: RUNG 2 · 2 clean & push press + 8 push-ups
items.detail: Bells go up, floor comes down. On multi-rep sets the bells do NOT go back to the floor between reps — clean once, then push press, dip and catch to the rack, push press again. Only the last rep gets lowered to the floor. That is the grip-endurance progression from the Olympic chain: same principle, less total hang time because your legs are doing the pressing now.

items.name: RUNG 3 · 3 clean & push press + 6 push-ups
items.detail: The middle rung, and where the block turns over. The bells are getting heavy and the push-ups are getting shorter — one is helping you and one is not. Keep the transitions tight; the time you lose in this block is time standing around between the bells and the floor, not time under load.

items.name: RUNG 4 · 4 clean & push press + 4 push-ups
items.detail: The crossover point — four and four. Rack position is where this falls apart: elbows in, bells resting on your forearms, breathe in the rack rather than rushing. Four push-ups should feel like a break by now, which is exactly the trade this ladder is built on.

items.name: RUNG 5 · 5 clean & push press + 2 push-ups
items.detail: The top of the ladder. Five unbroken push presses off one clean, then two push-ups and you are done — and then you go straight back to rung one and do the whole thing again. Note which ladder number it stops being fun, that is the number I want back.

blocks.text: This closes a hole that has been open since day one: your log has kettlebells, a treadmill, and floor core, and zero bodyweight strength. Ninety push-ups at your bodyweight is real pressing volume that costs your grip nothing, which is the exact currency you are short on — grip called the July 27th chain, not lungs. And the crossing structure means the block never settles into a rhythm: the half that is getting harder and the half that is getting easier swap places under you around rung three.

blocks.title: CORE · ANTI-ROTATION UNDER LOAD
blocks.meta: ~5 min · 2×40 lb + 16 kg · 3 rounds · 30s rest between rounds
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · straight through · your job is to NOT move, not to move more
blocks.workRest: Three rounds, 30 seconds between them. Both movements are about refusing to rotate or arch — you are already on the floor from the ladder, so this is a natural place to finish. Rotating off the last four core blocks: carries on Sunday, figure-8 and hollow on the 1st, chops and lateral walks on the 28th, overhead carries on the 27th. This one is anti-rotation from a plank plus anti-extension from your back, and the renegade row doubles as your horizontal pull for the day.

items.name: Renegade Row · 5/side
items.detail: 2×40 lb · both bells on the floor, hands on the handles, plank position with feet wide for stability. Row one bell to your hip while the other holds you up — and your HIPS DO NOT TURN. That is the entire exercise. If your hips rotate toward the rowing side, the rep does not count. Slow, alternating, five per side. Widen your feet if you are wobbling.

items.name: Dead Bug Pullover · 8 reps
items.detail: 16 kg · NEW to your log. Lie on your back, bell held straight over your chest with both hands, knees at 90 degrees. Press your low back FLAT into the floor and keep it there. Now take the bell back over your head toward the floor while extending the opposite leg straight out — bell and leg move away from each other, and if your back arches off the floor at any point you have gone too far. Come back, switch legs. Eight total. This is the anti-extension quality and it is the direct antidote to the low-back stiffness that keeps showing up in your check-ins.

blocks.text: Short block, and it is doing double duty — the renegade row is your only dedicated pull today and it is loaded at 80 pounds, and the dead bug pullover is the first true anti-extension floor drill in the program. Three rounds is enough after ninety push-ups.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~4 min · chest and shoulders from the push-ups, wrists from the floor, hips and calves from the quarter at 8.8
blocks.text: Walk 60s at 3.0 if you have not already. Then: doorway or floor chest stretch 45s/side — ninety push-ups plus overhead work will have your front side locked up · overhead lat and tricep stretch 30s/side · wrist flexor and extensor stretch 30s each direction, both hands on the floor then flip them over · standing calf stretch 30s/side · half-kneeling hip flexor 45s/side · thoracic extension over a rolled towel 45s · 5 slow nasal breaths. Report back with TWO things and only two: (1) in JERK SCHOOL, did the bells ever feel weightless at the top of the drive, yes or no — that single answer decides whether jerks get programmed as a real lift or go back to the shelf. (2) How many complete LADDERS you finished in the 13 minutes. Everything else is optional. And if you get a chance, the one that has been open since the 27th: on Sunday's carries, was it GRIP or BREATHING that called it first.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today. Use the COUNTDOWN twice: 13 minutes for the Crossing Ladder, and 90 seconds for each float in the Run Ladder. Use the STOPWATCH for nothing else — Jerk School has no clock at all, and the Run Ladder is measured on the treadmill's DISTANCE readout, not its timer.
